observation_summary: The StrBuilder.contains(char) and indexOf(char) methods were incorrectly iterating over the entire underlying buffer length instead of the actual size of the string builder, leading to false positives when searching for characters that existed in the buffer but were logically removed.
hypothesis: The methods were using the physical capacity of the buffer (thisBuf.length) as the loop termination condition instead of the logical size of the string (this.size), causing the search to scan beyond the valid string content.
prediction: The code would show a loop condition using 'thisBuf.length' which should be replaced with 'this.size' to correctly bound the search to the active string content.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff confirms that the loop termination condition in both 'contains' and 'indexOf' was changed from 'thisBuf.length' to 'size', which directly corrects the algorithmic iteration strategy.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a classic algorithmic error where the loop termination condition was incorrectly defined. It is not a missing check (Checking) because the logic was present but used the wrong boundary variable. It is not an assignment error because the logic of the loop itself was flawed. It is an Algorithm/Method defect because the procedure for searching the string was implemented with an incorrect iteration strategy.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the loop condition changed from 'i < thisBuf.length' to 'i < this.size'.
The bug report description explicitly states that 'thisBuf.length' was used where 'size' should have been used.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves a condition, it is not a guard or validation check; it is the primary loop termination condition for the search algorithm itself.
